subject: DPA / TIA delegation & UK addendum — Kepler evidence snapshot
messages:
From: Legal Team <legal@kepler.health>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA / TIA scope and subcontractor evidence request

Jordan —

Thanks for the call earlier. Kepler's procurement/legal team is working through final DPA sign-off and we have two outstanding asks before we circulate to our InfoSec board: a) confirmation of whether Redwood has delegated UK addendum obligations to the CloudGrid subprocessor (we saw mention of a delegated controller recommendation in your earlier deck), and b) a snapshot list of subprocessors that process EEA/UK data with exported routing (we need org-level contact and region).

Can you provide a redacted subprocessor list and a short TIA/DTIA summary that shows where the UK addendum is attached (and any outstanding DocuSign steps)? We can accept a redacted CSV + a short memo.

We're aiming to present to the board on Friday (9/10) and would like to validate by EOD Thursday if possible. Let us know if you need an NDA or additional info.

— Rachel (on behalf of Kepler Legal)
Legal Team
Kepler Therapeutics

Marissa / Kim — forwarding Kepler's ask. They want: redacted subprocessor list (EEA/UK routing + org contact), and a short TIA/DTIA summary that shows whether the UK addendum is delegated to CloudGrid (or remains with Redwood).

Kim, can you prepare the list and a 1-page memo summarizing the delegation model + any outstanding DocuSign steps? If CloudGrid requires its own attestation we should note that. If possible let's include: subprocessor name, country, primary contact, data path (EEA/UK/onshore fallback), and whether there is a signed addendum.

I'll reply to Kepler with the materials and propose a DocuSign link for the UK addendum if needed. Tight timeline — aiming for internal draft in ~3 hours.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA / TIA scope and subcontractor evidence request

Jordan / Marissa —

Attached are the items we can share immediately: 1) subprocessor_list.csv (redacted to org-level + routing column), and 2) tia_summary.pdf (2-page) which explains our standard DTIA approach and how the UK addendum is surfaced. Key points in the memo:
- Redwood executes SCCs/TIAs with customers; for UK customers we attach the UK addendum.
- Subprocessors are assessed; where CloudGrid provides infrastructure in the UK we have either delegated addendum or direct attestation depending on the subprocessor contract.
- For CloudGrid specifically: we hold a delegation agreement as of 2027-06-15 and their attestation (sample) is available upon request.

Attachments (stubs):
- subprocessor_list.csv (CSV, ~14KB) — columns: subprocessor, primary_country, contact, routing, addendum_signed (yes/no), attestation_available (yes/no)
- tia_summary.pdf (PDF, ~28KB) — short explanation + redaction guidance

I also generated a one-click DocuSign powerform link for the UK addendum if Kepler wants to sign through us; I put that link in uk_addendum-docusign-link.txt. That link is the standard commercial UK addendum we use (no redlines). If they need a modified addendum we'll need legal to review redlines (likely a 48–72h turnaround).

If Kepler needs CloudGrid's attestation itself, we request an NDA or the standard platform access form — CloudGrid restricts attestation distribution to downstream customers.

—Kim
Sr. Contracts Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: DPA / TIA scope and subcontractor evidence request

Hi Rachel / Kepler team —

Thanks for the note; attaching the redacted subprocessor list and a short TIA summary from our counsel. Quick summary below so your board has the essentials without opening attachments:

- Subprocessors: redacted list attached. CloudGrid shows routing through UK and WEU nodes; addendum_signed = yes, attestation_available = conditional (requires NDA).
- UK Addendum: standard Redwood UK addendum has been attached to the TIA where required. We can push a DocuSign powerform for Kepler to execute immediately: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?env=demo&acct=00000000
- DTIA / TIA: Redwood uses contractual TIAs for customers requiring explicit transfer impact analysis. The attached tia_summary.pdf highlights the mitigations (SSE, encryption-in-transit & at-rest, processor access controls, and our regional routing fallbacks).

Next steps we propose:
1) Kepler confirms whether CloudGrid attestation is required for your board (if yes we will route attestation request to CloudGrid — they typically require an NDA).
2) If Kepler is comfortable with redacted evidence + our TIA memo we can proceed to countersign the DPA (DocuSign link above).

Please confirm preferred path and any follow-up questions.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the attachments. We reviewed the redacted subprocessor list and TIA summary; board wants two clarifications before we sign: 1) a concrete fallback region if UK processing is unavailable (is Ireland an automatic fallback?), and 2) whether the standard SLA includes a 99.9% availability commitment for the dedicated inference endpoints (we need the SLA clause reference).

If you can confirm those two items in short form we can proceed with the DocuSign flow. Otherwise we may request CloudGrid attestation but prefer to avoid adding a vendor NDA step if possible.

—Rachel
Kepler Legal / Procurement
